top_story_title: Ransomware crews are exploiting the PAN-OS authentication bypass CVE-2026-0257 to get on VPNs
top_story_summary: Unit 42 updated its threat brief on CVE-2026-0257 on 19 October, naming ransomware operators Spikey Scorpius (also tracked as Qilin) and Tarnished Scorpius (also tracked as Inc) as active exploiters of the PAN-OS flaw. This is no longer a theoretical risk on a perimeter device: it is initial access tooling in the hands of groups whose next step is domain-wide encryption.
top_actions: Enumerate all PAN-OS firewalls and GlobalProtect portals from asset inventory, filtered by model and running version; confirm each against Palo Alto Networks' fixed-release table for CVE-2026-0257 (check the vendor advisory for the fixed release).
Upgrade on the vendor fixed build, HA pair secondary first, and treat this as an emergency change - the KEV due date of 2026-06-01 is already past.
Terminate all active GlobalProtect sessions and revoke session tokens after upgrade; assume stolen session cookies.
Rotate local firewall admin credentials, API keys, device certificates and VPN pre-shared keys - a pre-patch compromise survives the upgrade.
Remove management access (HTTPS/SSH/API) from any internet-facing interface and restrict it to a dedicated management VLAN or out-of-band network.
executive_summary: Ransomware operators Spikey Scorpius (Qilin) and Tarnished Scorpius (Inc) are actively exploiting PAN-OS authentication bypass CVE-2026-0257 to establish unauthorised VPN connections; the CVE is on CISA KEV with a 2026-06-01 due date that has already passed.
F5 shipped out-of-band patches for multiple NGINX flaws, three of them critical and leading to code execution - unscheduled work for anyone running NGINX as a reverse proxy or load balancer.
No fixed version numbers were stated in either source: confirm running builds against the vendor advisories rather than against any number quoted secondhand.
Check Point described an expanded AWS collaboration aimed at securing customers' AI workloads - tracked as a vendor AI defence, not as a vulnerability.
Quiet window otherwise: two of six collected items (a Plex Media Server exploit chain, a corporate espionage prosecution) are not network-infrastructure news and were dropped.
key_actions: **Palo Alto Networks** — Identify every PAN-OS device and GlobalProtect portal in the inventory and confirm the running version against the vendor's fixed-release table; check the vendor advisory for the fixed release.
**Palo Alto Networks** — Patch to the vendor fixed build as an emergency change, HA secondary first, and verify config sync after the upgrade.
**F5** — Inventory every NGINX instance - appliances, VMs, container images and sidecars - and record the running version; image-based deployments are the ones usually missed.

**F5** — Apply the F5 out-of-band patch to all units in the device group and verify config sync afterwards; check the vendor advisory for the fixed release rather than relying on a version quoted secondhand.

ai_defenses.solution: Check Point solutions on AWS Marketplace (expanded strategic collaboration with AWS for AI and cloud security capabilities)
ai_defenses.what_it_does: Check Point describes an expanded 2026 collaboration with AWS extending prevention-first security across cloud networks, applications, workloads and emerging AI environments, delivered through AWS Marketplace, with a stated focus on helping customers secure generative-AI initiatives built on AWS. The post names no individual product.

headlines.title: Threat Brief: Active Exploitation of PAN-OS CVE-2026-0257 (Updated October 19)
headlines.summary: Qilin and Inc ransomware crews are exploiting PAN-OS authentication bypass CVE-2026-0257 to stand up unauthorised VPN connections through the firewall.

headlines.title: F5 releases out-of-band patches for critical NGINX vulnerabilities
headlines.summary: F5 shipped out-of-band patches for multiple NGINX flaws, three rated critical, that can let an attacker execute code on vulnerable systems.

headlines.title: Check Point Expands Strategic Collaboration with AWS to Accelerate AI and Cloud Security Capabilities
headlines.summary: Check Point described an expanded AWS collaboration for 2026 focused on securing customers' generative-AI workloads alongside its cloud network and workload protection.
